## A telescope inside a natural medium {#markovs-idea}

:::::: {.panel-tabset}

### The idea, 1960

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
![](media/history/markov-lectern-author.gif){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 420px;" fig-alt="Moisei Markov speaking at a lectern."}

::: {.media-caption}
Moisei Markov.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**A large target already exists in nature.**

Place light sensors deep in a lake or sea.

Use Cherenkov light to reconstruct charged particles produced by neutrinos.

::: {.takeaway}
Instrument the medium instead of building the target.
:::

::: {.media-caption}
M. A. Markov, Rochester conference, 1960, p. 578.
:::
:::
:::::

::: {.column width="43%"}
![](media/history/markov-earlier.gif){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 350px; --media-width: 250px;" fig-alt="An earlier portrait of Moisei Markov from the INR anniversary archive."}

::: {.media-caption}

:::
:::

![](media/history/markov-pontecorvo.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 420px;" fig-alt="Moisei Markov on the left with Bruno Pontecorvo on the right."}

### Reines

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="49%"}
![](media/history/reines-cowan-1956.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 420px;" fig-alt="Frederick Reines at left and Clyde Cowan at the Savannah River experiment in 1956."}

::: {.media-caption}
Frederick Reines (left) and Clyde Cowan, 1956. Los Alamos National Laboratory.
:::
:::

![](media/history/reines-later.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 330px;" fig-alt="Frederick Reines, later portrait reproduced in Spiering's historical review."}

::: {.media-caption}

::: {.small}
Neutrino detection first; cosmic-neutrino astronomy next.
:::
:::
:::::

### Greisen

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="28%"}
![](media/history/greisen-portrait.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 320px;" fig-alt="Kenneth Greisen, portrait reproduced in Spiering's historical review."}

::: {.media-caption}
Kenneth Greisen. Undated portrait via C. Spiering.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="68%"}
**Greisen, Reines and Markov** discussed cosmic-neutrino detection in 1960.

Markov's underwater proposal supplied a practical route to a very large target.

::: {.question}
The physics was compelling. Could the instrument survive and work?
:::
:::
:::::
::::::

::: {.notes}
**3:00–4:15.** Present the idea first. The portrait tabs are optional material,
not four additional mini-talks. Select a pair if it helps the audience see the
long human timescale. The photo dates are not the dates of the scientific
proposals. The early Markov portrait is a small archival scan; do not invent
detail or an exact date. Reines and Cowan's picture documents the 1956 reactor
experiment, not an underwater telescope.

Source: C. Spiering, *Early History of Neutrino Astronomy and Neutrino Telescopes*,
GSSI 2024, slides 3–6. Markov, ICHEP 1960, p. 578. Photos and credits:
INR RAS anniversary archive and IceCube timeline; see media/history/SOURCES.md.
:::

## DUMAND: the first deep-ocean attempt {#pioneering-telescopes}

:::::: {.panel-tabset}

### People and ambition

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
![](media/history/dumand-1976.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 420px;" fig-alt="John Learned at the blackboard, Jed Hirota seated at left and Dick Davisson seated at right, DUMAND 1976 workshop."}

::: {.media-caption}
DUMAND workshop, 1976. John Learned at the board; Jed Hirota (left), Dick Davisson (right).
Photo: Anatoly Petrukhin, via IceCube.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="38%"}
**Deep Underwater Muon And Neutrino Detector**

Reines, Learned and colleagues pursued an ocean array near Hawaii.

A detector several kilometres below the surface needed entirely new engineering.
:::
:::::

### What the project taught us

```{=html}
<div class="timing">
<span class="time">1973–75</span><span>International discussions and the first workshops</span>
<span class="time">1987</span><span>A short prototype string operates from a ship</span>
<span class="time">1993</span><span>A deep-sea string deployment encounters a failure</span>
<span class="time">1995</span><span>US support ends before the planned array is completed</span>
</div>
```

::: {.takeaway}
Deployment, connectors, power and calibration became part of the physics problem.
:::

::: {.media-caption}
[IceCube historical archive](https://icecube.wisc.edu/about-us/icecube10/timeline/);
A. Roberts, *Rev. Mod. Phys.* **64**, 259 (1992).
:::
::::::

::: {.notes}
**4:15–5:00.** Spend most of the time on the workshop photograph. The project
helped create a community and techniques that outlived DUMAND. Its termination
was not an experimental refutation of the detection principle. Open the
timeline only if the chronology is useful.

Source: [Spiering 2024 historical talk](https://indico.gssi.it/event/632/contributions/2151/attachments/1298/2259/Early_History_of_Neutrinoastronomy_GSSI-29-09.pdf),
slides 13, 25–26. Photo attribution follows the IceCube archive caption.
:::

## Lake Baikal: the ice becomes a platform {#baikal-beginnings}

:::::: {.panel-tabset}

### Why Baikal?

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="57%"}
![](media/history/baikal-winter-2005.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 420px;" fig-alt="Winter work at Lake Baikal, in a photograph dated 2005 by the DLNP archive."}

::: {.media-caption}
Winter expedition, 2005. [DLNP JINR archive](https://dlnp.jinr.ru/chronograph/75/3258).
:::
:::
::: {.column width="39%"}
**Alexander Chudakov proposed the site.**

Deep, clear water close to shore.

A frozen surface for deploying and maintaining the detector.

::: {.takeaway}
The lake supplied both the target and a seasonal construction platform.
:::
:::
:::::

### The team

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](media/history/spiering-author.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 280px; --media-width: 210px;" fig-alt="Christian Spiering."}

::: {.media-caption}
**Christian Spiering**

His Zeuthen group joined in 1988.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="56%"}
Scientists, engineers and winter expeditions turned the proposal into a working array.

The 2006 Markov Prize recognised Domogatsky and Spiering for NT200+ and
high-energy neutrino astrophysics.
:::
:::::

::: {.media-caption}
[INR 2006 prize announcement](https://inr.ru/eng/markove/mark2006e.html).
:::

### Three strings

**NT36, 1993**

Three strings and 36 optical modules at Lake Baikal.

> “Congratulations for winning the 3-string race!”

Francis Halzen to Christian Spiering

::: {.small}
NT36, DUMAND's TRIAD and AMANDA: competing routes to a working array.
:::

### First neutrinos

```{=html}
<div class="timing">
<span class="time">1980–84</span><span>A dedicated laboratory, site studies and early strings</span>
<span class="time">1993–94</span><span>NT36: early neutrino candidates</span>
<span class="time">1996</span><span>NT96: a clear upward-going neutrino signal</span>
<span class="time">1998</span><span>NT200 completed with 192 optical modules</span>
</div>
```

::: {.takeaway}
Atmospheric neutrinos demonstrated that Markov's method worked in a lake.
:::

::: {.media-caption}
C. Spiering, historical review (2024), slides 29–31;
[Baikal detector paper](https://cds.cern.ch/record/323330).
:::
::::::

## The path to a cubic kilometre {#cubic-kilometre-scale}

:::::: {.panel-tabset}

### AMANDA

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="57%"}
![](media/history/amanda-team.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 420px;" fig-alt="German AMANDA collaborators with optical modules, from the collaboration's historical archive."}

::: {.media-caption}
AMANDA collaborators and optical modules. AMANDA Collaboration; photograph undated.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="39%"}
**Halzen, Learned, Price, Morse, Barwick and colleagues** explored polar ice.

Early shallow deployments suffered strong scattering from bubbles.

Deeper ice made directional reconstruction possible.
:::
:::::

### IceCube

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="57%"}
![](media/history/icecube-last-dom-2010.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 420px;" fig-alt="Deployment of the final IceCube optical module in December 2010."}

::: {.media-caption}
Final optical module, December 2010. IceCube/NSF, via the IceCube timeline.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="39%"}
**1999:** the cubic-kilometre proposal.

**2010:** the last of 86 strings.

**2013:** an astrophysical neutrino flux.

::: {.takeaway}
A working technique needed sufficient exposure to reveal the cosmic signal.
:::
:::
:::::

### The team

![](media/history/icecube-team-2004-05.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 440px; --media-width: 76%;" fig-alt="The IceCube construction team in the 2004–2005 season, in front of a drilling tower."}

::: {.media-caption}
First IceCube construction season, **2004–2005**. IceCube/NSF historical archive.
:::

### ANTARES

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="57%"}
![](media/history/antares-illustration.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 420px;" fig-alt="Artist's illustration of ANTARES and the Nautile submersible, not a photograph."}

::: {.media-caption}
Artist's illustration of ANTARES and Nautile. ANTARES material via IceCube.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="39%"}
**2008:** the 12-line detector is complete.

Long-term operation demonstrated precision neutrino detection in the deep sea.

ANTARES, NEMO and NESTOR supplied experience for KM3NeT.
:::
:::::
